relevance_reason: Reports 5 children from 4 families with biallelic SLC13A1 loss-of-function variants, skeletal dysplasia, short stature and/or scoliosis, and abnormal sulfate levels, with functional studies of the variants.

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) reported 5 children from 4 families with biallelic SLC13A1 variants, identified by exome or genome sequencing and GeneMatcher. All of them came to medical attention because of concern about short stature, and all had scoliosis and/or skeletal dysplasia. Two of 2 probands tested had reduced plasma sulfate and/or increased urinary sulfate excretion. The authors concluded that biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC13A1 are a novel cause of skeletal phenotypes in humans, with sulfate levels as a measurable biomarker.
quotes: 5 children from 4 families with biallelic variants in SLC13A1 and a skeletal dysplasia phenotype were identified

All probands presented with concern for short stature and were found to have scoliosis and/or skeletal dysplasia. A reduction in plasma sulfate level and/or increase in urinary sulfate excretion was detected in 2 of 2 probands evaluated.
Biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC13A1 are a novel cause of skeletal phenotypes in humans with a measurable biomarker.

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) described proband 1, a 3-year-old boy of European ancestry born to nonconsanguineous parents. He had bilateral developmental hip dysplasia that was braced until age 9 months and came to attention at age 2 years with increasing hip pain. He had proportionate short stature (z-score below -2 SD) and mild dysmorphic features: epicanthal folds, a flattened nasal bridge, and a short, anteverted nose. He also had tapered fingers and deep-set nails of the halluces. Pelvic x-rays showed delayed, stippled femoral ossification consistent with multiple epiphyseal dysplasia, and a spine x-ray showed mild anterior beaking of the lumbar vertebrae.
quotes: Proband 1 is a 3-year-old male who presented at 2 years of age with increasing hip pain and a history of bilateral developmental hip dysplasia requiring bracing until 9 months of age.

Physical examination was notable for a normal gait and proportionate short stature (z-score < −2 SD) with a normal upper:lower body segment ratio. He had mild dysmorphic facial features, including bilateral epicanthal folds, a flattened nasal bridge, and a short and anteverted nose.

Serial pelvic X-rays from age 9 months showed delayed and stippled femoral ossifications consistent with the diagnosis of multiple epiphyseal dysplasia. Lateral spine X-ray performed at 2 years of age demonstrated mild anterior beaking of the lumbar vertebra

findings.statement: In proband 1, trio exome sequencing by Tise et al. (2025) found compound heterozygous SLC13A1 variants: a paternally inherited c.34C>T (p.Arg12*) nonsense variant and a maternally inherited c.1343G>A (p.Gly448Asp) missense variant. The p.Gly448Asp variant was absent in the homozygous state from gnomAD v4.1.0, with 221 heterozygous alleles. p.Arg12* was seen 3,884 times in the heterozygous state and 7 times in the homozygous state. In MDCK cells, p.Gly448Asp completely abolished sulfate transport.
quotes: Trio exome sequencing identified biallelic variants in SLC13A1: paternally inherited NM_022444.4:c.34C>T p.(Arg12∗) and maternally inherited NM_022444.4:c.1343G>A p.(Gly448Asp).

Homozygous missense variants were absent from the Genome Aggregation Database (gnomAD v4.1.0) for variants NM_022444.4: c.1343G>A p.(Gly448Asp), NM_022444.4:c.1547T>C p.(Leu516Pro) and NM_022444.4:c.1744T>C p.(Tyr582His), with heterozygous allele counts of 221, 7, and 3, respectively.

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) found that proband 1 excreted more sulfate in urine than normal: his sulfate/creatinine ratio was 10.96 (reference 0.5-6.0). His heterozygous parents had normal values (father 1.71, mother 3.81). Plasma sulfate could not be measured because of inadequate specimen transport.
quotes: demonstrating elevated urinary sulfate excretion in the proband (sulfate/creatinine ratio 10.96; reference: 0.5-6.0) and normal urinary sulfate excretion in the parents (father: 1.71; mother 3.81)

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) described proband 2, a girl of Asian ancestry born to nonconsanguineous parents. Her legs were noted to be bowed when she began walking at about 14 months. At age 3 years she had tibial bowing and spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia, with small, fragmented proximal capital femoral epiphyses and wedge-shaped vertebral bodies. By age 11 the bowing had improved spontaneously, but she had developed mild scoliosis. At age 12 years her height was 137.7 cm (3rd percentile, z = -1.85) and her stature was proportionate.
quotes: Orthopedic evaluation at 3 years of age revealed tibial bowing and spondyloepiphyseal dysplasia with small and fragmented proximal capital femoral epiphyses and wedge-shaped vertebral bodies
When she was reevaluated at 11 years of age, her leg bowing had improved spontaneously, but she had developed mild scoliosis.
Most recent measurements at 12 years of age were 137.7 cm (3rd percentile, z = −1.85) and 42 kg (51st percentile, z = 0.02).

phenotypes.hpo_label: Hypoplasia of the capital femoral epiphysis

findings.statement: Trio genome sequencing in proband 2 did not find a cause in any known disease gene. Tise et al. (2025) then searched SLC13A1 specifically and found a homozygous c.1744T>C (p.Tyr582His) missense variant inherited from both parents. The variant was absent in the homozygous state from gnomAD v4.1.0, with 3 heterozygous alleles. In MDCK cells, it completely abolished sulfate transport.
quotes: However, a targeted search for variants in SLC13A1 identified a homozygous missense variant, NM_022444.4:c.1744T>C p.(Tyr582His), with biallelic inheritance.

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) found that proband 2, who was homozygous for p.Tyr582His, had a plasma sulfate of 0.107 mM (reference 0.3-0.5 mM). Her fractional excretion index of sulfate was increased (reported as 0.38 in the text; reference 0.17-0.34). Her plasma level was lower than the mean of 0.25 mM reported in heterozygous carriers of SLC13A1 nonsense variants, and similar to the 0.065 mM reported in a child homozygous for p.Arg12*. The authors took this as consistent with the missense variant being a loss-of-function allele.
quotes: Sulfate measurements in the proband showed an increased fraction excretion index of sulfate of 0.38 (reference: 0.17-0.34), and a reduced plasma sulfate of 0.107 mM (reference: 0.3-0.5 mM; mean among individuals with heterozygous SLC13A1 nonsense variants: 0.25 mM)
similar to the level reported in a child homozygous for the p.(Arg12∗) variant (0.065 mM)

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) described fraternal twins (proband 3, male; proband 4, female) born at 34 weeks to nonconsanguineous parents. Their skeletal surveys showed spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia that had been interpreted as consistent with Kniest dysplasia. Proband 3 had exaggerated thoracic kyphosis and lumbar lordosis, anterior beaking of the vertebrae, short and broad femoral necks, and metaphyseal flaring. He developed scoliosis that progressed from 12 degrees at age 4 years to an S-shaped 28-degree thoracic curve at 13 years. He also had pectus carinatum, a type 1 Chiari malformation, an atrial septal defect, and broad toes. Proband 4 had ovoid vertebrae with anterior wedging and widened metaphyses, along with broad thumbs, 2-3 toe syndactyly, and short, broad halluces. At age 10 years their heights were 129.6 cm (z = -1.66) and 134.4 cm (z = -0.85), respectively.
quotes: Several skeletal surveys were performed on proband 3 (Figure 1E-L), which showed exaggerated thoracic kyphosis and exaggerated lumbar lordosis, anterior beaking of several thoracic and lumbar vertebral bodies, short and broad femoral necks, and proximal and distal flaring of the femoral and tibial metaphyses, consistent with SEMD

which showed ovoid vertebral with anterior wedging, broad and short femoral necks, and widened metaphyses of tubular bones consistent with SEMD, interpreted as “numerous osseous abnormalities compatible with Kniest syndrome.” Her physical examination was significant for normal gait, broad thumbs, 2,3 toe syndactyly, and short and broad halluces.

At 10 years of age, the twins returned for evaluation of shorter than expected proportionate stature (proband 3 height 129.6 cm, 5th percentile, z = −1.66; proband 4 134.4 cm, 20th percentile, z = −0.85)

findings.statement: In the twins (probands 3 and 4), quad exome sequencing by Tise et al. (2025) found compound heterozygous SLC13A1 variants: a paternally inherited c.1547T>C (p.Leu516Pro) missense variant and a maternally inherited c.144G>A (p.Trp48*) nonsense variant. Earlier COL2A1 sequencing had found no variant. p.Leu516Pro was absent in the homozygous state from gnomAD, with 7 heterozygous alleles. In MDCK cells, it completely abolished sulfate transport.
quotes: Quad exome sequencing identified biallelic variants in SLC13A1 in both twins: paternally inherited NM_022444.4:c.1547T>C p.(Leu516Pro) and maternally inherited NM_022444.4: c.144G>A p.(Trp48∗).
Urine glycosaminoglycan analysis was within normal limits for proband 3, and COL2A1 sequencing did not detect any variants in either twin.

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) described proband 5, a boy born to nonconsanguineous parents, who was evaluated for scoliosis at age 14 years. He had proportionate short stature (157.3 cm, z = -2.13). Imaging showed thoracolumbar scoliosis, reduced height of several mid and lower thoracic vertebral bodies, and concave endplates, reported as suggestive of osteogenesis imperfecta or metabolic bone disease. He also had mild to moderate neurocognitive impairment, an atypical developmental disorder, Asperger's disorder, and anxiety disorders.
quotes: Proband 5 is a male and only child of healthy, nonconsanguineous parents who presented with concern for scoliosis at 14 years of age.

Radiographic imaging showed a 42° right thoracic and 26° left thoracic curve, diminished vertebral body height of multiple mid and lower thoracic bodies, and concave endplates, reported as “suggestive of osteogenesis imperfecta or metabolic bone disease”
Mild to moderate neurocognitive impairment affecting sensory, motor, attention, and subcortical abilities, atypical developmental disorder and Asperger's disorder

findings.statement: In proband 5, trio genome sequencing by Tise et al. (2025) found a homozygous c.144G>A (p.Trp48*) nonsense variant in SLC13A1, inherited from both parents.
quotes: Trio genome sequencing identified a homozygous nonsense variant in SLC13A1, NM_022444.4:c.144G>A p.(Trp48∗) with biallelic inheritance.

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) noted that in all families the SLC13A1 variants were biallelic, which they considered consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance. Heterozygous parents were healthy.
quotes: All SLC13A1 variants demonstrated biallelic inheritance, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance, and resulted in missense or nonsense changes.

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) built a homology model of SLC13A1 based on the SLC13A5 structure. It predicted the following effects of the missense substitutions: p.Arg237Cys loses most contacts and hydrogen bonds at the intracellular end of transmembrane domain 5; p.Gly448Asp introduces clashes within transmembrane domain 9; p.Leu516Pro removes contacts and introduces clashes in transmembrane domain 10, part of the ligand recognition pocket; and p.Tyr582His removes nearly all contacts in the extracellular C terminus.
quotes: The p.(Gly448Asp) substitution (G448D) is predicted to introduce a new contact with C37 in TM2, and introduce significant clashes with L66 and M72 (Figure 3D).
The p.(Leu516Pro) substitution (L516P) is predicted to remove most of these contacts and introduce clashes with the backbone of the helix at P512 and L513 (Figure 3F).
The p.(Tyr582His) substitution (Y582H) is predicted to remove all contacts and H-bonds other than with P583 (Figure 3H).

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) expressed SLC13A1 in stably transfected MDCK cells and measured [35S]-sulfate uptake. The missense variants p.Arg237Cys, p.Gly448Asp, p.Leu516Pro, and p.Tyr582His each abolished sulfate transport completely. However, each variant protein still reached the plasma membrane at levels similar to wildtype, suggesting the substitutions impair transport without abolishing trafficking.
quotes: All 4 amino acid sequence substitutions, p.(Arg237Cys), p.(Gly448Asp), p.(Leu516Pro), and p.(Tyr582His), led to complete loss of sulfate transport activity because no detectable [35S]-sulfate transport was present for mutants compared with the control wild-type mEmerald-SLC13A1 construct

The plasma membrane expression of each variant was examined using confocal microscopy and was similar to control mEmerald-SLC13A1 (Figure 4B-M), suggesting that these amino acid substitutions affect sulfate transport but do not appear to completely disrupt trafficking to the plasma membrane.

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) reported gnomAD v4.1.0 counts for the SLC13A1 variants. p.Gly448Asp, p.Leu516Pro, and p.Tyr582His were not seen in the homozygous state, with 221, 7, and 3 heterozygous alleles, respectively. p.Arg12* was seen in 3,884 heterozygotes and 7 homozygotes, and p.Arg237Cys in 3,129 heterozygotes and 5 homozygotes.
quotes: were observed in both the heterozygous and (rarely) in the homozygous state, with allele counts of 3884 heterozygous/7 homozygous; 3129 heterozygous/5 homozygous, respectively

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) noted that proband 5, who was homozygous for p.Trp48*, had a neurodevelopmental phenotype, and that a previously reported child homozygous for p.Arg12* had autistic features. They stated that more patients will be needed to determine whether SLC13A1 loss-of-function variants, or possibly only nonsense variants, are associated with a neurodevelopmental phenotype.
quotes: Proband 5 with homozygous p.(Trp48∗) exhibited a neurodevelopmental phenotype (Table 1), whereas a previously reported child with homozygous p.(Arg12∗) had autistic features.
Whether SLC13A1 LOF variants or possibly only nonsense variants, are associated with a neurodevelopmental phenotype will require identification and evaluation of additional individuals.

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) cited previous work showing that SLC13A1 is not expressed in cartilage or bone. On that basis, they proposed that the osteochondrodysplasia is secondary to the systemic metabolic disorder of sulfate homeostasis caused by loss of renal sulfate reabsorption, and that this disorder may affect other organ systems.
quotes: However, Neff et al reported that SLC13A1 is not expressed in cartilage or bone and concluded that the osteochondrodysplasia that results from the deletion of SLC13A1 was secondary to the underlying metabolic disorder, which likely affects other systems

findings.statement: Tise et al. (2025) suggested that oral sulfate supplementation, given directly or through sulfate sources such as N-acetyl-L-cysteine, warrants evaluation in humans. Because Slc13a1-deficient mice show enhanced acetaminophen hepatotoxicity, they advised caution in giving acetaminophen and other drugs metabolized by sulfation to individuals with biallelic SLC13A1 loss-of-function variants.
quotes: The use of oral sulfate supplementation, either directly or via other sulfate sources, such as NAC, to saturate other collateral sulfate transporters and any residual SLC13A1 function is an approach that warrants further evaluation in humans.

caution should be taken in the administration and dosing of acetaminophen and other medications metabolized via sulfation to individuals with biallelic SLC13A1 LOF variants until the full clinical phenotype is better understood

relevance_reason: First report of a patient with biallelic SLC13A1 loss-of-function variant causing hyposulfatemia with skeletal dysplasia.

findings.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) reported a Dutch boy, the only child of nonconsanguineous parents, who presented at 4 months with enlarged knees that could not fully extend, with normal length and head circumference. Skeletal survey at 6 months showed ovoid vertebral bodies, spiky widening of the metaphyses, irregular tarsal bones, slight rib flaring and somewhat small epiphyses that were more noticeable at 4 years; skull and pelvis were normal, and serum calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, PTH and 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 were normal. The radiologic abnormalities improved with age, so that at 11 years only flattening of the cervical vertebral bodies and irregular lumbar vertebral endplates remained.
quotes: He presented at 4 months with enlarged knees that could not fully extend, while his length (−0.5 SDS) and head circumference (+0.5 SDS) were normal.

Skeletal survey at 6 months of age revealed generalized skeletal abnormalities, particularly ovoid‐shaped vertebral bodies and spiky widening of the metaphyses but also irregular tarsal bones, slight flaring of the ribs and somewhat smaller epiphyses which became more noticeable at 4 years (Figure 1A,B).
The radiological abnormalities ameliorated and at 11 years, only flattening of the cervical vertebral bodies and irregular lumbar vertebral endplates remained (Figure 1C).

findings.statement: At 12 years the patient reported by van de Kamp et al. (2023) had enlarged knees and elbows, reduced movement in the lumbar spine and knees, winged scapulae, finger hypermobility and flat feet; height was normal (+1 SDS) but the trunk was relatively short (sitting height/height ratio -2.0 SDS). He had a slightly abnormal gait and could not run easily, sustained a forearm fracture at 8 years, and DEXA at 13 years showed BMD Z-scores of 0.2 in the lumbar spine and -2.1 in the proximal femur. Puberty began at 11.5 years, when his bone age was more than 1 year advanced.
quotes: At 12 years of age, he exhibited enlarged knees and elbows, reduced movement in the lumbar spine and knees, winged scapulae, hypermobility of the fingers and flat feet.
Although height was normal (+1 SDS with target height at +1 SDS) his trunk was relatively short, with a sitting height/height ratio of −2.0 SDS.
Dual‐energy x‐ray absorptiometry (DEXA) at 13 years showed bone mineral density Z‐scores of 0.2 in the lumbar spine and −2.1 in the proximal femur.
Pubertal onset (i.e., a testicular volume of 4 ml) occurred at age 11.5 years, the median age for Dutch boys. At this time, his bone age was more than 1 year advanced.

phenotypes.text: reduced proximal femur bone mineral density

findings.statement: The patient reported by van de Kamp et al. (2023) had above-average cognitive development without epilepsy, but autistic features including difficulty with social communication, restricted behaviors and interests, sensitivity to environmental changes and rigid thinking, frequently leading to panic attacks and school absenteeism. He had no joint pain, visual or hearing complaints, or skin abnormalities.
quotes: While the patients cognitive development was above average, autistic features such as difficulty with social communication, restricted patterns of behavior, interest and activities, an elevated sensitivity to changes in his environment and rigid thinking patterns were frequently leading to panic attacks and school absenteeism.
The patient experienced no joint pain, no visual or hearing complaints, and no skin abnormalities.

findings.statement: By exome sequencing in the patient, van de Kamp et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.34C>T (NM_022444.3) nonsense variant in exon 1 of the SLC13A1 gene, resulting in an arg12-to-ter (R12X) substitution, previously shown to cause total loss of function in Xenopus oocytes. The nonconsanguineous parents were heterozygous, and the patient had a 20-Mb region of homozygosity on chromosome 7q31.32, suggesting a common ancestor. The variant has a global allele frequency of 0.20%, and 1 homozygote is reported in gnomAD.
quotes: A homozygous g.122839967G>A (Chr7[GRCh37]), c.34C>T, p.(Arg12Ter) variant was identified in the first exon of the SLC13A1 gene (NM_022444.3). This variant causes a gain of stop predicted to result in a truncated protein and has previously been shown to cause total loss‐of‐function in Xenopus laevis oocytes.

The patient had a 20 Mb region‐of‐homozygosity on chromosome 7q31.32 containing both the SLC13A1 and the CFTR gene, while his parents were heterozygous for both variants, suggesting a common ancestor.

Arg12Ter and Trp48Ter, have a relatively high global allele frequencies (0.20% and 0.05%, respectively) and homozygosity for the Arg12Ter SLC13A1 variant is reported once in the Genome Aggregation Database

findings.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) noted that their patient also had cystic fibrosis, an incidental exome finding, due to a homozygous founder CFTR variant (c.1364C>A, p.Ala455Glu) located 5.6 Mb from SLC13A1 within the same region of homozygosity; he had mild CF with a sweat chloride of 64 mmol/L and stable lung function.
quotes: In addition, we found a known pathogenic homozygous g.117188849C>A (Chr7[GRCh37]), c.1364C>A p.(Ala455Glu) variant in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene (NM_000492.3).
Persistent fatigue and chronic cough were ascribed to cystic fibrosis (CF), an incidental finding of the exome sequencing which was confirmed by a sweat chloride measurement of 64 mmol/L.

findings.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) found severely reduced plasma sulfate (over 80% reduction) in the patient and a fractional sulfate excretion close to 100% (reference 13-34%), consistent with complete loss of renal sulfate reabsorption. Both heterozygous parents had plasma sulfate below the control range, and the mother had a fractional sulfate excretion of 45%.
quotes: Plasma sulfate levels were severely reduced in the patient and also below the control range in both parents (Figure 2 and Table S1).

Reference values for Fractional Sulfate Excretion (FEsulfate) range from 13% to 34%, whereas the patient's FEsulfate was close to 100%, while his mother had an FEsulfate of 45% (Figure 3 and Table S1).
We found an FEsulfate close to 100%, consistent with complete loss of renal sulfate reabsorption in our patient, as well as an over 80% reduction in plasma sulfate levels.

findings.statement: In the patient, van de Kamp et al. (2023) found reduced serum cholesterol sulfate (443 ng/ml; reference 500-1236 ng/ml), whereas other serum steroid sulfates were normal and urinary steroid metabolome was age-appropriate. The percentage of chondroitin sulfate disaccharides in urinary glycosaminoglycans did not differ from parents and controls.
quotes: Serum cholesterol sulfate was reduced in the patient (443 ng/ml; reference range 500–1236 ng/ml), while other serum steroid sulfates were within the reference range (Table S3).
The percentage chondroitin sulfate disaccharides in urinary glycosaminoglycans did not differ significantly in the patient, the parents and the controls (Table S2).

findings.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) administered intravenous N-acetylcysteine (133 mg/kg bolus over 60 minutes, then 133 mg/kg over 8 hours) to the patient; plasma sulfate normalized during the bolus and maintenance infusion but returned to baseline 15 hours after stopping. Erythema during the bolus resolved with clemastine. The authors advised avoidance of acetaminophen because of potential risk of hepatotoxicity.
quotes: Plasma sulfate concentrations normalized after bolus injection of NAC and during maintenance infusion but returned to baseline 15 h after stop of the infusion (Figure 4).
A bolus of 133 mg/kg NAC (Fluimucil®) was administered intravenously in 60 min, followed by 133 mg/kg in 8 h in analogy to the treatment of acetaminophen intoxication.
Although the patient's transaminase levels were normal on multiple occasions, he has been strongly advised to avoid acetaminophen.

findings.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) noted that SLC13A1 loss-of-function variants R12X and W48X have relatively high global allele frequencies (0.20% and 0.05%) and hypothesized that biallelic loss-of-function variants are more common than recognized and may present later in life with degenerative bone and joint disease, with mild presentations escaping diagnosis.
quotes: We hypothesize that biallelic SLC13A1 loss‐of‐function variants are more common and may also present later in life with degenerative bone and joint disease but that mild presentations escape diagnosis unless radiological evaluation is performed in childhood.

findings.statement: van de Kamp et al. (2023) noted that homozygous SLC13A1 loss-of-function variants occur naturally in Texel sheep and miniature Poodles, both with skeletal dysplasia including stunted growth, enlarged joints, joint stiffness and early-onset osteoarthritis, while the Slc13a1-null mouse shows hyposulfatemia, hypersulfaturia, growth retardation, behavioral abnormalities and seizures.
quotes: Remarkably, homozygous loss‐of‐function variants in SLC13A1 have occurred naturally in two animal breeds, the Texel sheep and the miniature Poodle, both with evident skeletal dysplasia, including stunted growth, abnormal stance and locomotion, enlarged joints, joint stiffness and early‐onset osteoarthritis.
The SLC13A1−/− mouse also exhibits behavioral abnormalities, impaired memory and reduced brain serotonin levels in addition to spontaneous clonic seizures.
